thread: FOI 2026-036 — schedule of all Great House Farm / Church Farm records and 1875–1915 registers
subject: FW: 2026-036- Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
note: The two schedules in this email were tables; their cells are shown one per line as they appear in the plain-text email.
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request.

Amgueddfa Cymru has previously responded to requests concerning Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough, including FOI 2026-024 and FOI 2026-032. In responding to the present request, further enquiries were undertaken with Archaeology, Industry and Social History Collections. These enquiries built upon the searches already undertaken for the earlier requests.

Collections staff reviewed records identified through references to Great House Farm, Ty Mawr and Llandough Farm, Llandough (Vale of Glamorgan), together with records returned through associated place-name searches. Records relating to the wider Llandough area, to other locations sharing the name "Llandough", or to other properties bearing the name "Great House Farm" were reviewed but were not considered to relate to the location specified in your request.

Question 1
A schedule of every object, archive file, accession, loan, enquiry or correspondence record that Amgueddfa Cymru holds which is indexed, provenanced or otherwise recorded as from Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Vale of Glamorgan).
The schedules provided in response to FOI 2026-032 contained the records previously identified as relating to the location specified in your request.
The additional enquiries undertaken for this request identified the following records:
Reference
Title
Date
Description
Ref 13.2
Waterwheel from Llandough Farm
Collected 1 April 1979
Waterwheel collected from Llandough Farm. Museum records state that the item was donated by Wales and West Housing Association in connection with development of the site. The item was never formally accessioned and has subsequently been deaccessioned.
MS 3360/3
Particulars, Conditions and Plans of the Sale of Nine Well-Known Farms in the Vale of Glamorgan forming part of the Llandough Estate
1924
Photostat copy. Collections staff identified a page relating to Great House Farm within the document. Provided in FOI: 2026-032
No further records relating specifically to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough were identified.

Question 2
The same schedule for Church Farm, Llandough, but only insofar as records were retrieved during the searches undertaken for FOI 2026-024 and can be identified without a new full search.
The record identified is:
Reference
Title
Description
63.24
Archaeological accession
Details attached
No further records were identified from the material retrieved during the searches undertaken for FOI 2026-024.

Question 3
Any accession, register entry, day-book, donations book or correspondence in the collections of Amgueddfa Cymru or of its predecessor Cardiff Museum / Welsh Museum of Natural History / National Museum of Wales, dated 1875-1915, recording ironwork, armour, a visor, a lance, a helmet, "armour from Llandough", or a find from Great House / Llandough Farm.
No such records were identified.

For clarification, the accession registers maintained by Cardiff Museum form the earliest accession registers of the National Museum of Wales collection. Objects held by Cardiff Museum were not re-accessioned when responsibility for the collections transferred to the National Museum of Wales and the accession numbering sequence continued uninterrupted. Searches of the earliest accession registers therefore encompass the former Cardiff Museum accession records.

As part of the enquiries undertaken in response to this request and previous requests concerning the same location, accession records and associated collections documentation were reviewed for the objects and locations specified above. No accession record, register entry, day-book entry, donations book entry or correspondence dated between 1875 and 1915 relating to finds from Great House Farm, Ty Mawr or Llandough Farm was identified.

Question 4
Any object record for Llandough ironwork that is not labelled "visor" or "lance" but is or was associated with the farmhouse floor or rear wing / dairy.
No such records were identified.

Archaeology Collections have confirmed that they hold no record of any additional ironwork from Llandough associated with the farmhouse floor, rear wing or dairy beyond material already considered in previous responses concerning this location.

I hope this information is helpful.

If you are dissatisfied with the way your request has been handled, you may request an internal review. Requests for an internal review should be submitted within 40 working days of the date of this response.

If you remain dissatisfied following the outcome of the internal review, you have the right to apply directly to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) for a decision. The ICO can be contacted at www.ico.org.uk.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

thread: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-036 – response of 5 October 2026

Thank you for the letter. I note the additional records identified (Ref 13.2 waterwheel and the page of MS 3360/3).

What remains unanswered
On 27 September I corrected the place names in the FOI 2026-032 pack, identifying at least PAS 2022.18.1 (NGR SS9934672805) and a separate Great House Farm entry at Llandow as belonging to different properties. Your reply of 28 September accepted the distinction: the collections system does not group by similar names, no recorded cross-attribution is held, and those hits arose from the search rather than catalogue overlap.

The 5 October letter does not supply a cleaned / filtered schedule showing which of the FOI 2026-032 items survive that filter. Until that is provided, the cross-reference still carries the Cowbridge and Llandow material. That is the point left open on 28 September and still open now.

What you have not said
You have not stated, item by item, which of the earlier schedule entries are now excluded as relating to Great House Farm near Cowbridge or Great House Farm, Llandow. You have not confirmed the parish of the page of MS 3360/3 that you identify as relating to Great House Farm (which Llandough, and any vendor / tenant / acreage / parcel detail that identifies the holding). You have not confirmed whether Ref 13.2 (waterwheel collected 1 April 1979 from “Llandough Farm”, donor Wales and West Housing Association) is recorded as the Penarth site opposite the hospital, or as the farmhouse demolished by BP on 6 December 1988.

Please therefore supply:
1. A filtered schedule of the FOI 2026-032 records that remain after exclusion of all items relating to Great House Farm / Llandough near Cowbridge and to Great House Farm, Llandow. For each surviving entry: accession or archive number, title, date, and one-line description.
2. Explicit parish confirmation for the page of MS 3360/3 identified as relating to Great House Farm: which Llandough, and any vendor / tenant / acreage / parcel detail that identifies the holding.
3. Confirmation whether Ref 13.2 is recorded as the Penarth site opposite the hospital, or as the farmhouse demolished by BP on 6 December 1988.

These are requests for recorded information already within the searches undertaken. I am not seeking new searches or opinions. The unanswered point is the filter that you accepted was necessary on 28 September but have not yet applied in a disclosed schedule.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

In relation to the filtered schedule, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate recorded document identifying, item by item, which search results were excluded following review. Search results were reviewed by staff to determine whether they related to the location specified in your request, and the outcome of that review was reflected in our response of 5 October 2026. We do not hold a separate audit schedule of those decisions.

In relation to MS 3360/3, the relevant page was previously supplied in response to FOI 2026-032. That page records that "Great House" formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924, was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, comprised approximately 202 acres, was situated in the Parish of Llanfair, and describes the homestead as being situated in the Village of Llandough. No additional recorded information identifying the holding has been identified within the material reviewed.

In relation to Ref 13.2, the collections record describes the item as a "Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)". No further location information has been identified within the record.

We trust this clarifies the position.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

thread: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: Re: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
FOI Team,

Thank you for the clarification.

Your email of 7 October materially clarifies the position, and I have now corrected my records to distinguish the different Llandough farmsteads.

Ref 13.2 — Llandough Farm opposite the hospital

I understand and accept the distinction in your catalogue description:

“Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)”

This refers to the separate Llandough Farm in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality, not to Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr. I am not seeking to attribute the waterwheel to Great House Farm.

I will therefore treat Ref 13.2 as a separate Llandough Farm record unless a primary Museum record expressly establishes otherwise.

MS 3360/3 — Great House / Llandough Estate

The more significant clarification is the information you have now supplied from MS 3360/3.

You state that the page records that:

- “Great House” formed part of the Llandough Estate sale particulars of 1924;
- it was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons;
- it comprised approximately 202 acres;
- it was situated in the Parish of Llanfair; and
- the homestead was situated in the Village of Llandough.

Those particulars provide a much more specific identification than the earlier catalogue description.

I am particularly interested in the combination of Llandough Estate + Parish of Llanfair + Village of Llandough + approximately 202 acres + W.G. Thomas & Sons.

Could you therefore confirm one narrow point from the record already examined:

Does the MS 3360/3 page or plan itself contain any further recorded identifier which identifies which historical Llandough is meant — for example the specific place-name form, neighbouring farms, estate owner, parish/benefice wording, acreage breakdown, plan number, tenant information, road, church or other geographical feature?

I am not asking the Museum to make a new identification or to provide an opinion. I am asking only whether such information is actually recorded in the page or plan you have already examined.

There is an important reason for keeping this distinction precise. There are two different farmsteads in the Llandough near Penarth/Cardiff locality relevant to the Museum's records:

1. Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, beside St Dochdwy's Church; and
2. Llandough Farm, separately described by the Museum as “opposite hospital”.

They must not be treated as alternative names for one farm.

There is also a separate question concerning the Museum's wording “Llandough Church Farm” in the 1858 provenance of accession 63.24. I now understand that this should not automatically be equated with either of the above merely because it contains the word Llandough. Unless the underlying historical evidence expressly identifies the 1858 “Church Farm”, I will continue to record that identity as unresolved.

Filtered schedule

I also accept your clarification that the Museum does not hold a separate recorded audit schedule showing, item by item, which search results staff excluded after reviewing the results.

I therefore do not ask the Museum to create such a schedule.

For the purposes of the record, I will instead distinguish between:

- records positively identified as Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr;
- records positively identified as the separate Llandough Farm opposite the hospital;
- records from other Llandoughs, including Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge;
- and source-specific records whose location remains unresolved.

The new MS 3360/3 particulars are sufficiently distinctive to make the underlying page and plan an important identification source, so I would be grateful for confirmation of whether any further geographical identifier is actually recorded there.

Thank you again for the clarification.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler

thread: FOI 2026-024 / 032 / 036 — outstanding item 7 (recorded basis for “unrelated / not in scope”)
subject: FOI 2026-024 / 032 / 036 – outstanding item 7: recorded basis for treating already-found records as “unrelated / not in scope”
body:
Dear FOI Team,

Thank you for the disclosures under FOI 2026-032 (22 September) and 2026-036 (5 October).

On 25 August 2026 you stated that searches had located records of “other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm” which were withheld as “not in scope”. On 26 August I asked for those records and, specifically, the recorded basis for calling them unrelated (item 7).

That question remains unanswered. The later disclosures released certain Church Farm and other-site material but still did not supply the internal note, search-log entry or other record that justified the original classification.

I therefore request:

1. The recorded basis (search log, file note, email or other document) that led the Museum to treat the already-found Great House Farm / Church Farm records as unrelated or out of scope on 25 August 2026.
2. If no such written basis exists, an explicit statement to that effect.
3. Confirmation that the full set of records located in the August searches has now been disclosed or, if any remain withheld, the precise exemption relied upon for each.

Please treat this as a request for the information that should have been provided under the internal review of 2026-024. This is for the completeness of the evidence library on the public record.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Dear FOI Team,

FOI 2026-036 — your letter of 7 October 2026

Thank you. I note three points from that letter.

1. You do not hold a separate recorded document listing, item by item, which search results were excluded. Please state which systems were searched for that schedule (collections database, search-export, review log, email, paper file) and whether a physical file was retrieved, and by whom and on what date. A not-held answer is incomplete without that (FOIA s.16).

2. MS 3360/3: the page already supplied records Great House as part of the 1924 Llandough Estate sale particulars, occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, about 202 acres, Parish of Llanfair, homestead in the Village of Llandough. Please confirm whether the catalogue or the page itself names which Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth or Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge). If that is not on the page or in the catalogue entry, say so.

3. Ref 13.2 is recorded as a waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital). I treat that as the Penarth hospital site, not the farmhouse demolished on 6 December 1988, unless a further recorded field says otherwise.

I am not asking for a new search or for a document you say you do not hold. I am asking for the systems searched and the physical-file check on the not-held point, and the parish identification if it is already on the page or catalogue entry.

Cofion,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: FOI 2026-024 / 032 / 036 — outstanding item 7 (recorded basis for “unrelated / not in scope”)
subject: RE: ALLANOL/EXTERNAL - FOI 2026-024 / 032 / 036 – outstanding item 7: recorded basis for treating already-found records as “unrelated / not in scope”
body:
Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

In relation to your request for the recorded basis on which records were treated as outside the scope of FOI 2026-024, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate search log, file note, internal note or other recorded document setting out the rationale for that assessment.

The original response was based on searches which identified no records relating to the reported discovery described in your request, namely the alleged discovery of a soldier, horse remains and associated armour at Great House Farm, Llandough. While searches identified records relating to other archaeological finds from Church Farm and archaeological investigations at Great House Farm, staff concluded that those records did not relate to the specific discovery described in your request and therefore fell outside its scope. No separate record of that assessment was created. We have since provided you with the records referred to as being from Church Farm.

No records remain withheld.

Cofion cynnes,

thread: FOI 2026-036 — filtered schedule, MS 3360/3 and Ref 13.2 (follow-up)
subject: RE: FOI 2026-036 – Great House Farm, Llandough – filtered schedule still not supplied; unanswered points from FOI 2026-032 correction
body:
Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

In relation to the "filtered schedule", as previously explained, Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold a separate recorded document identifying, item by item, which search results were excluded following review. The review was undertaken by staff using the records and search results identified during the handling of the request. No separate audit schedule, review log or equivalent record of exclusion decisions was created.

In relation to MS 3360/3, following further review we have confirmed that the page previously supplied does not relate to the property that was the subject of FOI 2026-036. While the document refers to a property known as "Great House", it relates to a holding in the Parish of Llanfair and not to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff), which was the subject of your request. The document should therefore be regarded as outside the scope of FOI 2026-036.

We do not hold any further recorded information linking MS 3360/3 to Great House Farm/Tŷ Mawr, Llandough (near Penarth/Cardiff).

In relation to Ref 13.2, our position remains unchanged. The collections record describes the item as a "Waterwheel from Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)". No further location information has been identified within that record.

We have no further recorded information to provide in relation to these matters.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales
